text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Troops free hostages in Peru: Judge, two soldiers die as four-month standoff ends in gunfire; all rebels killed.
- Fujimori bolsters tough-guy image: Pride is first for President.
- Flood panic grows in Manitoba: Premier declares state of emergency.
- Reform organizer quits over remarks: Party acts on comments about Sikhs.
- Ottawa to develop national home-care program: Federal contribution likely 'millions,' Health Minister says.
- NorTel rings up record profit: Jump in revenue accompanies 'terrific' earnings from growth in wireless, private networking.
- Dow roars back to life with 173-point gain: Earnings, falling yields provide lift.
- Black reaps dividend windfall: Hollinger chairman to gain $69-million from special payment.
- Traders: Last call on the TSE floor.
- Laidlaw cuts ties to waste: US$376-million sale completes the Ontario firm's exit from solid waste operations.
- Tobacco's Big Three go to bat against Ottawa's ad restrictions.
